cal.title: Plan calendar (Google Calendar / iPhone)
cal.intro: Turns your plan into a calendar subscription URL: each session is an all-day event (the past 2 weeks to 8 weeks ahead) titled with the session name, ✓ in front when done and ✗ when missed; the event holds the duration, load, the steps and an "open this session in the plan" link. Edits, moves to another day and deletions follow (rest days and blocked days don't appear).
cal.secret: The URL is the key: anyone with it can read your plan without logging in, so don't share it publicly. If it leaks, press "Reset URL" and the old one stops working at once.
cal.reach: The URL uses the address you opened this page at. Google Calendar must be able to fetch it from the internet (e.g. through a Cloudflare Tunnel); an app that only runs on localhost can't be reached by Google, and the iPhone needs to reach it too.
cal.copy_fail: Couldn't copy automatically: select the URL and copy it by hand
cal.confirm_reset: After a reset the old URL stops working at once: remove the old subscription in Google Calendar / on the iPhone and subscribe again with the new URL. Reset now?
cal.confirm_disable: After turning it off, subscribed calendars no longer update. Turn it off?
cal.done_reset: New URL created; the old one no longer works
cal.google: Open Google Calendar on a computer; next to "Other calendars" on the left, + › "From URL", and paste the subscription URL.
cal.google_lag: Google decides on its own how often it fetches the URL again (usually every few hours, up to about a day) and it can't be forced, so a change you just made won't show in Google Calendar right away.
cal.iphone: Settings › Calendar › Accounts › Add Account › Other › "Add Subscribed Calendar", and paste the URL (or tap the webcal URL on the iPhone).
cal.iphone_lag: In Settings › Calendar › Accounts › "Fetch New Data" set it to every 15 minutes: a change then shows in about 5–15 minutes.
cal.iphone_widget: Add the Calendar widget to the Home Screen to see today's session; the link in the event opens that session's editor in the plan (log in to this site the first time).
thr.title: Threshold tests (LTHR / AeT / CP)
thr.help: One row per test; it applies from the test day on and never to earlier days. HR load, power load, the easy-run cap, the interval gate and the plan's heart-rate / power targets all use it. Max and resting heart rate are under "Max / resting heart rate" below.
thr.est_loading: Estimating LTHR / AeT from your runs…
thr.how_aet: AeT test (Uphill Athlete): after a 10-min warm-up, run 40–60 min at a steady power on a treadmill or flat ground (the plan schedules 40 min; UA advises no shorter than 40 min). Heart-rate drift < 5% between the halves means that heart rate is below the aerobic threshold; step up test by test until the drift is about 5%.
thr.how_lthr: LTHR test (Friel): a 30-min solo all-out run; the average heart rate of the last 20 minutes.
thr.how_cp: Pick the CP test under "CP test" above (quick 20-min all-out / standard 12 min + 30 min rest + 3 min / a 5–10 K race); test every 4–6 weeks or 10–21 days before a race. The CP is computed automatically (a PD-model fit to the upper edge of your 90-day power curve): a test is one all-out effort on that curve, there is nothing to apply. Without a CP typed here, the plan uses the modelled threshold power of the PD model on your Stryd power (fitted to the upper edge of the mean-max curve of every run in the last 90 days, CP tests included; 30–60 min power; a new fit replaces the CP only when it differs by 3 W or more). A CP typed here wins.
thr.pz_src: Source: {src}. Palladino: zones describe training, they are not for prescribing it. Near threshold is not an official zone name; it is the top of 3B.
thr.pz_stryd_src: Source: {src}. The zones the Stryd app and PowerCenter show, worked out here from the same CP. An easy run's 65–80% CP is Stryd Zone 1.
thr.pz_model_help: Which zone set the plan's power targets use (automatic planning, the session steps, what goes to the watch); the charts' power zones default to it too. Each kind of session keeps its intensity and takes the nearest level of the set: easy runs, long runs and long mountain days take the set's easy level, a recovery run is capped at the top of the level holding 75% CP, intervals and climbs take the level that overlaps their band the most. After a switch the coming sessions are re-planned and the ones on the watch are re-sent by the plan's rules; a power target you set yourself in a structure (% CP, a zone, watts) stays, steps left on "auto" follow the new set. Personalized zones need a power–duration model from your Stryd runs of the last 90 days; without one the plan uses Palladino.
thr.pz_model_saved: Plan power zones saved: the coming sessions are re-planned with them
thr.pz_personal_basis: What the zones stand on: modelled threshold power {w} W · fitted {date} · data {from} – {date} (Stryd runs of the last {days} {days|day|days}). The % column is % of the modelled threshold power, W is watts.
thr.now: In use: AeT {aet} / LTHR {lthr} / CP {cp} W
thr.cp_src: (CP: {src}; the same one the plan uses)
thr.hist_h: Threshold changes: which threshold changed on which day
thr.hist_intro: The plan's heart-rate and power ranges follow these thresholds. When a session's ranges differ from the last session of the same kind, look at the entries between the two dates.
thr.lthr_default: ⚠ LTHR is the comparison folder's factory default (never entered), so the zones are off too: enter a test result below or apply the estimate
thr.wko5: Settings in the comparison folder: running LTHR {lthr}, max heart rate {mhr}
thr.wko5_default: — this is the comparison folder's factory default (dated {date}, i.e. never entered). Its heart-rate zones = zone table × LTHR, so zones from the default are off too.
thr.est_cross: Cross-check: heart rate {hr} at CP ±3% power ({n} {n|time|times})
thr.est_aet_none: You rarely have steady, easy runs of 45 minutes or more, so the data can't give one. An Uphill Athlete AeT test is the most accurate (see "How to test").
thr.est_confirm: Set {name} to {v}? A row dated today is added and zones and HR load from then on are recalculated with it.
thr.conf_tip_none: No signal that the value is wrong, but no test has confirmed it either (estimate).
thr.chk_tt30: 30-min test on {date}: mean HR of minutes 10–30 {v} bpm; 30-min mean power {p} (vs CP {cp})
thr.chk_hrmax_test: Max-HR test on {date}: highest HR held ≥ 5 s {v} bpm (spikes filtered)
thr.chk_cand: Candidate: highest HR held {hold} s {v} bpm ({date}, estimate)
thr.chk_confirm: Set {name} to {v} bpm (from {date})? Zones and workout HR targets will be recalculated
pmc.title: Starting chronic / acute load
pmc.help: Chronic load / acute load need a starting point. Order: your value (from its date) → automatic (the mean daily load of the first 28 days with training load, used for both chronic and acute load) → 0. The overview, the charts, the chronic load ramp guardrail and the load balance < −30% of chronic load recovery week all use the same one. A manual value restarts the training load chart on its date; before that date the automatic start applies. Only needed when you have a few weeks of data here but know your chronic / acute load at that time from another platform (e.g. TrainingPeaks).
pmc.auto: Automatic: mean daily load of the first {n} {n|day|days} with load {seed} (from {date})
pmc.auto_open: ; fewer than {days} {days|day|days} so far, it changes with new data
pmc.now: Today ({date}) chronic load {ctl}, acute load {atl}, load balance {tsb}: the overview, the charts and the guardrails use these
pmc.ignored: The manual value's date {date} is after today: not used yet (automatic)
pmc.need: Fill in the date, chronic load and acute load
pmc.saved: Saved; the overview and charts are recalculated
race.title: Race result (E pace)
race.help: Kuo-Feng Hsu's 90-minute test is run at E pace, worked out from one race result (Daniels' VDOT formula; E pace = the speed at 62–70% of VDOT, matched to Daniels' pace table, an estimate). Enter your latest all-out road or track race (5 K to marathon); trail races don't count, the climbing distorts the time. Used only for the 90-minute test and its explanation; other sessions and zones are unchanged. A race older than 180 days is too old (estimate): the 90-minute test doesn't use it and goes by your CP test or the talk test instead. Race results are one list shared with the running-experience questionnaire: a race saved here or confirmed with "Use this race" is added to it, and the E pace uses the newest road race in the list.
race.k_act: A race confirmed from your activities ({date} {title})
race.k_survey: The race from your running-experience questionnaire ({date})
race.stale: The race was {d} {d|day|days} ago, which is too old (over {n} {n|day|days}, estimate): the 90-minute test doesn't use it and goes by your CP test or the talk test; update it when you have a new race result
race.none: No race result yet: the 90-minute test uses power (with a tested CP) or the talk-test pace instead
race.cands: Activities from the last 180 days that look like road races (trail races are not listed). One is used only after you press "Use this race":
race.need: Fill in the distance, the time (e.g. 45:00 or 1:35:20) and the date
race.saved: Saved; the 90-minute test's E pace follows
hr.title: Heart rate
hr.help: Max HR, in this order: the value you enter → the watch's value (COROS account) → the best 10-s average HR in your runs of the last 365 days (optical-HR spikes filtered out first) → the age formula 208 − 0.7 × age (an estimate). Resting HR: the value you enter, else the watch's (COROS account). Both are used for heart rate reserve (HRR) and max-HR zones. Entered values apply from today; earlier charts keep the values of the time.
hr.model_help: Only sets the HR targets of workouts (auto-planning, workout steps, pushing to the watch): recovery run Z1, Easy run / long run / trail Z2, tempo Z3, threshold Z4, Supra / VO2max Z5. "Auto" goes by which numbers are believable: a believable LTHR → lactate threshold zones; else a believable max HR and resting HR → heart rate reserve zones; else max HR zones. You are told once when it switches. Picking one model keeps it. A measured AeT (AeT test) is always the Easy run cap. The activity review (easy / moderate) and auto-adjust (easy run too hard) use the same Easy run cap: an average HR up to the cap + 3 counts as easy. Without max HR or resting HR, lactate threshold zones are used. Each chart picks its own HR zones; this setting does not affect them.
hr.watch_none: Watch: not read yet (log in to COROS or sync once)
hr.model_saved: Saved; workout HR targets will be recalculated
hr.cmp_same: Close to your watch settings (every gap within {bpm} bpm), nothing to change ✓
hr.cmp_zones: HR zones ({model}): the gap compares each zone's upper edge
hr.cmp_read: The watch's values were read at the sync on {day}.
hr.cmp_hist_note: Every sync reads the watch account's values and adds an entry only when one changed; the change happened between that sync and the one before.
hr.cmp_hist_none: Nothing recorded yet. From now on every sync reads the watch account's values and adds an entry when one changes.
pv.title: My zones
pv.help: The zones the plan, the activity review and the charts use by default — only the units in use: heart rate always, pace while a session runs by pace, power only while power is in effect. Change the numbers under Thresholds and tests on the left; pick how the zones are built under Manual overrides.
pv.hr_none: No LTHR or max HR yet, so no zones: enter one under Heart rate or Threshold tests below.
pv.pw_none: No CP yet, so no power zones.
tl.help: A workout's "Training load" end condition is entered as this app's training load and converted to COROS TL (Training Load) when pushed to COROS. The default coefficients come from one runner's activities (estimate, error about ±20%); after a sync brings new activities they are refitted on your own COROS activities that have TL once 7 days have passed since the last estimate (at most once a week, together with Advanced › auto-estimated parameters; press "Re-estimate now" there to do it at once): recent activities weigh more, activities before a big threshold change (CP / LTHR) are left out, and with little data only a simple model is used, pulled toward the default (weight = n ÷ (n + 30)). New coefficients replace the old ones only if they are no worse on the last 30 days of activities.
tl.load: ; Load steps calibrated from your data ×{f} (n={n})
sync.ev_relogin: Login expired; logged in again automatically with the remembered password
sync.auth_lost: Login expired, please log in again
sync.cred_note: Without “Remember password”, your password is sent only when you log in and is not kept; only the encrypted login token / cookie is. With it ticked, the password is kept too, encrypted with the server's key on the server, for the automatic re-login. The same for every source you log in to with a password.
sync.background: Sync new activities in the background
sync.background_help: The server checks your watch account for new activities in the background now and then; a new one is synced and the overview, the plan's session matching, the activity classification and the charts you looked at lately are computed in the background, so a page opens up to date. An account used lately is checked about every 30 minutes, one used less often every 2–6 hours, and after a month without use only the daily sync is left. No checks from 1 to 5 a.m. Accounts are spread out and synced one at a time, so the site does not slow down; when COROS holds requests back, the next check waits longer. Garmin allows one automatic sync a day, so it is not checked in the background.
sync.background_plan: Your plan syncs once a night; no background checks for new activities.
sync.background_off: Background sync is off on this server.
sync.remember_coros: The password is encrypted with the server's key and kept on the server; unticking or logging out deletes it at once. When ticked, an expired login (24 hours) or a refused token logs in again once, automatically.
sync.remember_garmin: The password is encrypted with the server's key and kept on the server; unticking or disconnecting deletes it at once. When ticked, a token Garmin no longer accepts logs in again once, automatically (it counts toward the daily syncs; not while Garmin has the login locked).
sync.remember_tp: The password is encrypted with the server's key and kept on the server; unticking or logging out deletes it at once. When ticked, a token that can no longer be renewed logs in again once, automatically.
sync.remember_next: The password will be remembered at the next login (encrypted on the server)
rpe_load.summary: “Training load” by RPE (estimate) — load per hour: {levels} ({src})
rpe_load.src_default: the default is a general rule, ±{err}%; no rated activity yet
rpe_load.help: A workout's “Training load” can also be entered by feel: pick Easy / Somewhat hard / Hard / Very hard / Max (Borg CR-10 2 / 4 / 5 / 7 / 10) and the minutes; load = that level's load per hour × the hours. Each level's default is a general rule following Coggan's published formula: load per hour = intensity² × 100 at the level's intensity (ranges after Seiler's three zones by session RPE and Coggan's power levels, the points estimates) — not tuned to anyone. Each athlete's own values come only from their own rated activities (the RPE the watch recorded or COROS's post-run rating) and their actual load, level by level: from 3 activities per level, pulled toward the default while there is little or old data; a higher level never gives less, and a level changed only for that, with no data of its own, is marked “adjusted to the neighbouring level”. Planning targets only: the overview and the training load chart always use the watch's recorded load, never corrected by RPE.
rpe_load.calib_title: “Training load” by RPE: load per hour of each level
rpe_load.calib_tip: The defaults are a general rule (Coggan's published formula, load per hour = intensity² × 100, the intensity points estimates), not tuned to anyone; each athlete's values come only from their own rated activities. Tags: yours n = their own data, default (estimate) = the general rule, adjusted to the neighbouring level = no data of its own, changed so that a higher level never gives less.

calib.intro: These numbers are estimated from your data: after a sync brings new activities they are re-estimated once 7 days have passed since the last estimate (at most once a week); press the re-estimate button below to do it now. With too little data a default from the literature or an estimate is used. Click a label (or hover) for its explanation; set one by hand only when you are sure.
mode.admin_only: Only admins see this section, a tool for testing the formulas; switching changes only your own screens and calculations. Everyone else always uses "My formulas".
mode.only_mine: Data corrections, excluding broken activity files and the threshold test log apply only in "My formulas"; "Comparison mode" always uses the settings in the comparison folder.
general.title: Basic info
general.missing: Still missing: {list} (used to calibrate the calculations)
general.help: The few things the data cannot tell and only you know. Weight is used for W/kg, running economy (RE), the power calculator; each day uses the weight entry on or before it. Here you edit the newest entry (saved with the date you enter; an entry of the same day is replaced, the older ones stay). What you type wins: weight sync (Data sync tab) never changes it, and never overrides it with measurements of that day or earlier. Sex sets the anaerobic capacity prior (women 6.4, men 13.1 kJ) and the energy estimate; age is used for the energy estimate and, without a max heart rate, for the uphill heart-rate cap (220 − age, an estimate). The birth year is stored, so the age goes up by one each year. The power meter (Stryd / none) is under Equipment on the Training basis tab. Everything else is estimated automatically.
general.no_weight: No weight yet: enter your weight and save (used for W/kg, running economy (RE) and the power calculator)
general.wko5: Comparison folder data: height {h} cm, sex {sex}, weight log {list}
general.saved: Saved; the charts will be recalculated with the new weight
general.exp_history: You have 4+ weeks of running on record: the plan follows your record, so the running-experience questions aren't needed.
general.exp_intro: Used to plan your first month; every question can be left blank and the weekly volume is used as entered. Once you have 4 weeks or more of activities, the plan goes by them instead.

hints.title: How many tips
hints.intro: How much explanation and how many reminders a page shows. Tips that change what you should do or concern safety (a red pain light, a plan change waiting for you, a cut-off time) show at every level; the others go under “Details” as chosen here. A page shows at most 3 reminders; the rest fold into “N more reminders”.
hints.full_note: Explains where every number comes from; for new runners and first-time users
hints.standard_note: Explanations only when they apply, the rest under “Details”; what most people use
hints.lean_note: Only tips that change what you do or concern safety; for experienced runners who know to eat before a session, walk the steep bits and mind wet trails
hints.why_new: — no 4 weeks of running on record yet and your answers say you are starting out, so Full for now
hints.suggest: You have a running record, a race in the last year and runs over 2 hours: the tips may be more than you need — switch to Lean?
hints.load_failed: Couldn't read the tip level; using Standard
sugg_declined.title: Tests no longer suggested
sugg_declined.intro: Tests you said “No thanks” to in the suggestion box are not suggested again in any week. Press Restore to have the box suggest them again when they are due.
sugg_declined.restored: Restored: the suggestion box will suggest the {test} again
syncfail.title: Activities that failed to download
syncfail.help: Activities whose download or import failed during a sync are listed here; later syncs retry just these instead of listing every activity again. Each is retried automatically at most 5 times or over 7 days of trying, then it stops; press Retry to try again. Manual entries without a FIT file are listed too; press Retry once a file exists.

syncfail.started: Sync started; it tries this one again
syncfail.queued: The next sync tries this one again
synccheck.help: Lists every activity on the watch / platform and compares it with the data here by activity id: the ones the platform has and this app does not can be fetched with Download missing (only those); the ones only here are listed, never deleted; the ones still on the failed-download list are listed too. COROS takes about 40-60 s; the same source cannot sync meanwhile, and the sync position does not change. While automatic syncing is on (sync on open or a daily time), the last 60 days are also checked every week and missing activities are downloaded; TrainingPeaks workouts that were planned but never done are counted apart and never downloaded.

debug.title: Debug API (for AI agents)
debug.help: Lets an AI agent, or your own local copy, read activities, the plan, thresholds and the sync state, or export the settings and the plan, over HTTPS with a personal token. A token with "change settings" (write:config) can also change thresholds, events and plan preferences: previewed before it is applied, every change logged and undoable; everything else is read-only. The token is shown once and the server keeps only its hash.
debug.enable_help: When off, every address under /api/v1/debug/ answers 404. Only the dedicated tokens work, never the web session; at most 60 calls per token per minute.

debug.scope_read_sync: Sync results and the error log

arch.title: Activity retention
arch.help: Activities older than the retention lose their FIT original and per-second cache in an automatic cleanup on the 1st of each month, between 3 and 5 a.m., without notice. Each activity's metrics, the training load chart, best efforts, achievements and Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) summits stay in its summary, so the long-term charts do not change; the activity list still shows it, marked “Archived — original file removed”, but its single-activity charts can no longer be opened. Activities the current thresholds or plan tests use are kept for now. Download your files first if you want to keep the originals.
arch.intro: FIT originals past the retention are removed every month; summaries, the training load chart, best efforts and achievements stay.
arch.skipped: The last cleanup ({date}) was postponed: the first import is still being filled in, it will try again
arch.last_none: Last cleanup: {date}, nothing past the retention
arch.last: Last cleanup: {date}, {n} removed ({from} to {to}), {mb} MB freed
arch.kept: ; {n} more used by a threshold or plan test, kept for now
arch.download_help: Packs every FIT original you synced or imported into one zip. Available any time, independent of the cleanup. With many files it takes a moment to start.
arch.free_cap: The free plan keeps the last year at full resolution, then only the summaries; a subscription can keep 2, 3, 5 or 10 years.
arch.cap_notice: Heads-up: the free plan keeps 1 year at full resolution. From the cleanup on {from}, activities older than a year keep only their summary (it was {was} {was|year|years}). Download your files first to keep the originals, or subscribe.
device.title: Offline data on this device
device.help: Without signal, Overview, Schedule and the activity list open from what this device keeps (read only). It is kept in three tiers: P0 must have (Overview, Schedule), P1 should have (activity list, achievements), P2 when there is room (the single activities of the last 30 days you opened); 20 MB in total at most, and over it P2 goes first, then P1. It refreshes by itself when online. Each device and browser keeps its own copy, deleted on sign-out.
device.intro: Overview and Schedule open from here without signal. See how much is kept and whether the browser may delete it.
device.usage_over: Over the budget: this number counts everything this site keeps on this device. When the offline data is over it, P2 goes first, then P1.
device.p0_what: Overview, Schedule (today, this week and the next weeks)
device.p2_what: The single activities of the last 30 days you opened (charts and cards); none is kept ahead
device.state_partial: Partly kept ({n} {n|item|items} missing, retried when online)
device.state_empty_p2: None yet: open an activity of the last 30 days and it is kept
device.persist_yes: Yes: the browser won't delete it when the device runs low on space
device.persist_no: No: the browser may delete it when the device runs low on space (it is kept again once online)
device.persist_denied: The browser said no. Chrome and Safari decide by themselves: using the site often, adding it to the home screen or installing it as an app makes it more likely.
device.persist_na: This browser can't ask for persistent storage
device.updated_note: Refreshed by itself when online: P0 every 15 minutes, P1 every 6 hours, P2 when you open that activity online
device.a2hs_title: Add to the home screen so it isn't deleted after 7 days
device.a2hs: In an iPhone / iPad browser tab, Safari deletes the offline data kept here after 7 days without opening this site; opened from the home screen it doesn't. Tap Share → Add to Home Screen, then open it from the home-screen icon. The home-screen app keeps its own data, separate from the tab: the first time, sign in again there if the site asks, and the offline data is kept again there.
acct.title: Account
acct.pwc_intro: To change your password, enter the current one first. The new password needs at least 10 characters; don't use your email or a common password. Once changed, every other signed-in device is signed out; this one stays signed in.
acct.pwc_fill: Enter your current password and a new one.
acct.pwc_mismatch: The two new passwords don't match.
acct.pwc_done_out: Password changed; {n} other signed-in device(s) were signed out.
acct.export_intro: Everything you entered (settings, season plan, schedule, notes, injury log, uploaded GPX) and the activities and original FIT files you synced or imported, in one zip, with your account details and consent history. Sign-in credentials and remembered passwords are not included. With many files the download takes a moment to start.
acct.analysis_intro: Accepting the terms at sign-up also agreed to your data being de-identified and used in cross-user analysis to improve the algorithms. You can withdraw at any time. No cross-user analysis uses any data yet.
acct.withdrawn: Withdrawn: later analyses will not use your data.
acct.links_intro: Other services you sign in to with the same Google account. Once linked, the service can read what is listed below — never your activities, heart rate or other health data. Unlink here at any time and it can no longer read anything.

acct.link_no_google: Accounts that sign in with email can't be linked with Cairn yet; sign in with Google to link it

acct.unlinked: Unlinked: {name} can no longer read your data.

wsync.title: Weight sync (Apple Health)
wsync.help: Lets the iPhone Shortcuts app or Health Auto Export send the weights in Apple Health. A token can only send weights: it reads nothing and opens nothing else; it is shown once, the server keeps only a hash, and you can revoke it any time.
wsync.intro: A web app cannot read Apple Health, so the iPhone sends it: make a token, set up the Shortcut below, and from then on opening your scale's app sends the latest weight.
wsync.rules: Every weight received is kept, and they are sorted out once a night at {at} (nothing is recomputed when one arrives): one value per day, the day's last; a new weight entry only when it differs from the weight in use that day by ≥ {d} kg, or the previous entry is {g} {g|day|days} old or more; a weight you typed in Basic info wins, and measurements of that day or earlier never override it. W/kg, RE and the plan's power targets are recomputed only after an entry is added.
wsync.name: Name
wsync.confirm_revoke: Revoke “{name}”? Shortcuts using it will stop working.
wsync.confirm_all: Revoke every token? All Shortcuts will stop working.
wsync.st_superseded: a later one the same day
wsync.st_small: under {d} kg and under {g} {g|day|days} since the last entry
wsync.sc_1: Press “Make a token” above and “Copy” (the token is shown only this once).
wsync.sc_2: On the iPhone open the Shortcuts app › Shortcuts › ＋ (top right), and name it “Weight sync”.
wsync.sc_3: Add the action “Find Health Samples”: type “Weight”, sort by “Start Date”, “Latest First”, limit “1”.
wsync.sc_4: Add the action “Format Date”: the date is the health sample's “Start Date”, date format “ISO 8601”, “Include ISO 8601 Time” on.
wsync.sc_5: Add the action “Get Contents of URL”: the URL above; method “POST”; one header, key “Authorization”, value “Bearer ” followed by the token (one space after Bearer); request body “JSON” with three fields: kg (Number) = the sample's “Value”, unit (Text) = the sample's “Unit”, time (Text) = the “Formatted Date”.
wsync.sc_6: (Suggested) add “Show Result” and press ▶ once: you should see “Received 1 weight value…”, and the value appears under “Latest measurements received” here. The first run asks to read health data and to connect to this site: allow both.
wsync.sc_7: Automation: Shortcuts › Automation › ＋ › “App” › pick your scale's app (e.g. Withings, Garmin Connect, Zepp Life, or Health), tick “Is Opened” and, suggested, “Is Closed” too (closing it after the app wrote the new weight into Health sends that weigh-in), choose “Run Immediately”, turn off “Notify When Run”, then pick “Weight sync”.
wsync.sc_8: While the iPhone is locked no app may read health data, so trigger it on opening / closing an app, not at a fixed time. Sending the same value again is not counted twice.
wsync.hae_1: Needs Premium. Automations › ＋ › “REST API”: URL = the address above; Headers: “Authorization” = “Bearer ” + the token; Data Type “Health Metrics”, only “Weight & Body Mass” in Metrics; Export Format “JSON”; Date Range “Since Last Sync”.
wsync.hae_2: Press “Manual Export” once to test. It runs only while the phone is unlocked and is delayed in Low Power Mode.
wsync.proxy: If the site sits behind another sign-in layer (e.g. Cloudflare Access) the phone's requests are stopped there: ask the admin to open just this one address (the token is still checked), or send that layer's service token from the Shortcut as well.

power.watch: Power models also use watch-estimated power
power.watch_help: By default only Stryd power goes into the power models; without a Stryd, heart rate is used. Turned on, watch-estimated power is also used for the race power model (power curve, PD model), for Power load, for the power review of intervals, and, when LTHR is estimated from your runs, for telling which runs were hard enough. The CP of the plan and the charts does not change: it is still fitted on Stryd power only, or taken from a CP test you enter. Watch power reads on another scale than a Stryd, so a CP fitted on it can be much higher and the plan's power targets would be wrong. A watch-power run's Power load is divided by that same CP; without a CP it comes from pace or heart rate as before. To train by watch power: add a row under "Threshold tests" with the CP of a CP test done with watch power, so the plan and the test use the same kind of power. Watch power's accuracy has not been validated; treat the numbers as estimates.
backup.help: Packs the database (activities, schedule, settings, injury log and so on) and the files you changed (season plan, calibration, notes, chart views, route names, uploaded GPX) into one zip in the backup folder set below. That folder is on the server (the machine running the app); backups are not downloaded to your phone or computer. Logins and remembered passwords for the data sources (COROS, Garmin, TrainingPeaks, intervals.icu) are not included. If the server has a cloud-drive folder (iCloud Drive / OneDrive / Google Drive / Dropbox), pick it and that drive's sync client uploads the backups; the app never signs in to any cloud account. Keeps one a day for the last 7 days plus one a week for the last 4 weeks and deletes older ones — only backup files this feature made; nothing else in the folder is touched.
backup.restore_help: Pick a backup in the backup folder, or upload a backup file from your device; its contents and database integrity are checked first. Before restoring, the current database and files are saved to backups in the app folder on the server (also listed, so you can restore them back), then replaced with the backup's; files the backup does not hold are left alone, and share links are not restored. Afterwards, reload the page to see the restored data (the server needs no restart; the charts are recalculated, so the first page takes longer). Not overwritten: the backup settings on the server (folder, daily automatic backup), the plan calendar address, the Debug API, and the data-source logins (COROS, Garmin, TrainingPeaks, intervals.icu) — logins are not in backups, so after restoring on another server you log in once. Encrypted backups from older versions (.zip.enc) cannot be restored.
backup.fit_help: The synced FIT files (fit in the app folder on the server) go into the backup gzip-compressed, which makes it much larger. Leaving this off is fine: FIT files can be synced again from COROS / TrainingPeaks later. A restore only adds the FIT files the server does not have yet; existing ones are not overwritten.

askai.title: AI Q&A
askai.help: Use “Ask AI” to ask about the card, chart, session or calculator result you are looking at. Answers use only the app's own numbers and rules, and each part says whether it is an app rule or an AI inference. Only summaries are sent to the model (the status card's rule results, the last 8 weeks' totals, that card's text), never a GPS track. For now only the site's own account can use it, with its own API key; model calls cost money, there is a daily limit, and the same question gets the saved answer.
askai.enable: Turn on AI Q&A (“Ask AI” at the bottom right of every page)
askai.key_help: Stored encrypted; only the last 4 characters are shown, and it is never written to the log. When the server sets TRC_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or _FILE), that one is used.
askai.bad_key: That does not look like an API key
basis.equip_help: The one question: do you have a power meter. With a Stryd and a CP test or race in the last 42 days, the flat hard sessions and road easy runs go by power; with the CP stale or no power meter they go by heart rate / pace. Watch-estimated power is no power meter (its scale differs from Stryd's). A change re-plans the sessions and re-sends the watch at once.
basis.equip_sub: The only question; everything else is automatic. Power is used for the flat hard sessions only with a power meter and a CP tested in the last 42 days.
basis.equip_watch: The "watch-estimated power" chosen before is no power meter: it now counts as no power meter (the stored setting is unchanged).
basis.equip_saved: Equipment updated: the plan is re-planned for the new state and re-sent to the watch
basis.sport_help: Decides which charts the analysis shows, how the automatic plan is built and the race calculator's default; "What you train by now" on the right follows it too. Trail: climbing, descents, the course constant, steep power hiking and B2B all show. Road / marathon: the climbing and descent charts are hidden in favour of flat aerobic efficiency, HR drift, long-run distance and marathon-pace volume; the plan has no steep power hiking or B2B, and the Build long run gets a marathon-pace segment. The plan preferences on the Plan page change the same setting. Automatic = the next A races first: only trail races or Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) → trail, only road races → road; both → the harder one (race size, then predicted time, then EP), a tie or no answer → trail; no A race → the B races the same way; none → the share of trail + hiking time in the last 12 weeks (≥ 25% is trail, an estimate). C races don't count.
basis.sport_saved: Main sport updated: the plan preferences and the other pages follow it
basis.aetp_help: The test decides what is planned and how it is read; the interval gate decides when Zone 5 opens. The 90′ long-run test goes on the weekend long-run day (a Taiwanese coach's), the others follow "AeT test on". Planned only when needed: the pooled estimate is unreliable or drifting, about 6 weeks without a readable run, or after 4+ weeks off (an estimate). Start below 25 °C.
basis.aetp_auto: Automatic (Kuo-Feng Hsu 90 min; UA 40 when the long-run day has no room)
basis.cpp_help: Quick 20′: 20 min all-out, about 37 min; CP ≈ 0.95 × 20-min power, about ±3%, no anaerobic capacity. Standard 12′ + 3′: 12 min + 30 min rest + 3 min, about 70 min; a two-point CP plus anaerobic capacity, the most accurate; the rest can't be shortened. A race: a 5–10 K race or time trial, nothing extra planned; Riegel conversion (extrapolated), no anaerobic capacity. Every 4–6 weeks or 10–21 days before a race.
basis.hr_edit: Enter your own max and resting heart rate
basis.ovr_help: Everything is automatic by default; there is usually nothing to change here. A changed item says "(manual)" with "Back to automatic" beside it, and the kinds of session it touches say "(manual)" in "What you train by now" too. Without a power meter the power choices don't show; a power setting chosen before is kept, not deleted — choosing Stryd again brings it back.
basis.ovr_sub: Automatic by default; a changed item says "(manual)", and so does the result card.
basis.basis_help: Whether the plan's targets are heart rate or power. Automatic: by kind of session — see "What you train by now" on the right. With a power meter and a valid CP, road easy runs, long runs, flat intervals and hill repeats on 3–8% grades go by power (heart rate as a safeguard); trail easy runs, mountain long days and recovery runs by heart rate; steep power hiking by heart rate or RPE; long climbs and downhills have no target. With the CP stale or no power meter, what went by power goes by heart rate. Heart rate: heart-rate zones throughout. Power: power zones throughout (tests and downhills keep their own rules; with the CP stale or no power meter heart rate is used anyway). Only the sessions the system plans; any step can still be changed in the session's structure.
basis.climb_help: Trail only. What the race sessions exported from the race calculator send to COROS on runnable grades (−3 to +15 %, not technical legs or high altitude). With a Stryd (these legs are power): power by default; Effort Pace sends Effort Pace instead (COROS's grade-adjusted pace, the same conversion as the calculator's flat-equivalent pace). Without a power meter it is always Effort Pace, so this doesn't show. Garmin is unchanged: add a GAP (grade-adjusted pace) field on the watch for reference.
basis.saved: Saved: the coming sessions follow the new setting
basis.now_help: Read-only and automatic: follows your equipment, whether the CP is stale, the main sport and the manual overrides. Each kind of session shows its target now; ? says why. When the state changes (the CP going stale, say), the plan is re-planned and re-sent to the watch.

basis.st_cp_never: No CP test or race yet
basis.pw_paused: Power zones: the CP is stale, paused (one CP test brings them back)
coach.edit.basis_prefs: Changed the targets basis or a test method (Training basis)
